market_context: United States and Canada; safe maintenance of tank water heaters, including electric and gas shutdown procedures.
title: How to Flush or Drain a Water Heater

seo.title: How to Drain and Flush a Water Heater Safely
seo.meta_description: Drain and flush a tank water heater safely, remove loose sediment, and refill the tank before restoring power.
seo.search_intent: Drain or flush a tank water heater safely and know when an older or problematic unit should be serviced professionally.

excerpt: Shut off the water heater’s energy source, let the water cool, close the cold-water inlet, and connect a hose to the drain valve. Open a hot-water faucet to admit air and drain to a safe location. Before restoring power to an electric tank, confirm that the tank is completely full.
content_html:
Flushing a tank water heater is meant to carry out some of the sediment that settles at the bottom. The idea is straightforward; the risk comes from working with a container full of hot water that is also connected to electricity or gas.

Sequence matters: shut down the energy source first, control the water second, and only then put the heater back in service.

Make sure you have a tank-style heater

This procedure is not for a tankless heater. Tankless units are usually descaled through a different service procedure. Find the manual for your exact model before starting.

Turn the heater off and let the water cool

Stored hot water can cause severe burns. Shut the heater down in advance and allow it to cool according to the manufacturer’s instructions. For an electric unit, turn off the correct circuit. For gas, use the shutdown procedure specified for the appliance.

Close the cold supply and prepare a safe drain path

Attach a suitable hose to the drain valve near the bottom of the tank. Route the other end to a drain or location that can safely handle the water without flooding the home or damaging landscaping.

Close the heater’s cold-water inlet and open a hot-water faucet in the house. The open faucet lets air enter while the tank drains.

Open the drain valve gently

Open it slowly. If little or no water comes out, do not beat on or force an old valve. Sediment can clog the outlet, and a brittle valve can break.

Rheem recommends professional help when a drain valve will not open, leaks, or the unit is old and heavily fouled. The goal is maintenance, not turning a stable old heater into an emergency leak.

Draining and flushing are not quite the same

Draining removes water. Flushing also tries to move loose sediment out. Some manufacturers instruct owners to briefly reopen the cold-water supply during the process to stir sediment and carry it out through the hose. Follow the procedure for your model rather than improvising.

Refill completely before restoring power

Close the drain valve, remove the hose, and reopen the cold-water inlet while leaving a hot faucet open. Air may sputter at first. Once the flow becomes steady, let it run briefly and then close the faucet.

Do not energize an electric tank until you know it is full. Heating elements can fail quickly if they are powered while exposed to air.

Check for leaks before you leave

Dry the drain valve and any fittings you handled, then watch them for several minutes. A valve that starts dripping after maintenance needs attention.

Many manufacturers use annual flushing as a general reference, although hard water, usage, and the model can change that schedule. A successful flush ends with a full tank, no leaks, and a normal restart—not with a rushed sequence.

faq.question: How often should a water heater be flushed?
faq.answer: It depends on the model, water hardness, and use. Many manufacturers use about once a year as a general maintenance interval.

faq.question: Do tankless water heaters get flushed the same way?
faq.answer: No. Tankless units generally require a separate descaling procedure.

faq.question: What if no water comes out of the drain valve?
faq.answer: Do not force it. Sediment may be blocking the valve, and an older valve can break. Consider professional service.

faq.question: When can I turn an electric heater back on?
faq.answer: Only after the tank is completely full and a hot-water faucet is flowing steadily without trapped air.
